items.title: PDL-CUL-23-013, Cultural Drivers of Tourism Grant Funding Recommendations
notes:
Helen Chimirri-Russell, Director of Cultural Services, provided a brief overview of the grant program and the reasoning for the funding recommendations as set out in report PDL-CUL-23-013. She noted that there were applicants from all over the Region and the recommended recipients were determined using Council's approved grant guidelines. She further noted that two organizations, Cambridge Highland Games and Oktoberfest, have received the amount that was granted to them in the past as per the guidelines, however, both organization will be slowly transitioned out of receiving that level of funding. She explained that Cultural Drivers of Tourism Grant Funding is an incentive program not operating funding, so that is the reason that art galleries with current operating funding agreements with the Region do not qualify for this grant.

In response to the Committee, Helen Chimirri-Russell explained that there were two organizations were denied funding because they are currently receiving Regional funding, such as the Major Arts and Cultural Grant Program, and one organization did not qualify as their work did not relate to cultural activities. Staff will continue promote the grant program to expand the organizations that are applying.

The Committee discussed amending the proposed Staff recommendation to include Public Art Galleries as potential recipient for Regional grant funding, however, it was determined that direction to Staff would be more appropriate as the report is a separate issue.

Recessed at 11:58 a.m. and reconvened at 12:41 p.m.

items.title: Strategic Focus – Healthy, Safe and Inclusive Communities
CSD-HOU-23-022, ROWCHI Property Ownership Transfer to the Region of Waterloo
notes: Peter Sweeney, Commissioner of Community Services, provided a brief overview of the ROWCHI property ownership transfer as set out in report CSD-HOU-23-022. He explained that municipalities are not permitted to hold mortgages, so ROWCHI was created to hold the ownership to the listed properties until such a time as the mortgage could be closed. Staff determined that closing the mortgages on these properties was prudent in order to prevent the Region on paying increased interest rates.

items.title: Shelter System Statistics
notes:
Based on discussions during the Administration and Finance Committee meeting, P. Sweeney provided the shelter system statistics as requested. He identified that approximately 10% of individuals that access the shelter system are Refugees or Asylum Seekers, which would represent about 55 individuals. He also identified that during the week of August 6, 2023 there were 16 families accessing the shelter system out of which 7 families were Refugees. He expressed concern that there were 5 individuals that accessed the shelter system that were Refugees/Asylums Seekers in April 2023 and that number increased to 57 during July 2023. Additionally, Cambridge Shelter Corp had more intakes of Refugees and Asylum Seekers in July than in the previous 11 months combined. Regional Housing Stability Staff are meeting regularly to coordinate efforts with the Settlement Sector, which are responsible for settlement services, however, the system is fractured resulting in the increase in refugees and asylum seekers requiring access to the shelter system.

In response to the Committee, P. Sweeney confirmed that the Best Western has 120 available that are Regionally funded.

motions.item_title: CSD-HOU-23-022, ROWCHI Property Ownership Transfer to the Region of Waterloo
motions.text: That the Region al Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the proposed property ownership transfer from the Region of Waterloo Community Housing Inc. to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo as set out in report CSD-HOU-23-022 dated August 15, 2023: Accept the transfer of ownership effective December 31, 2023 or sooner if practicably possible, of two (2) community housing properties comprising 92 units in total at the following addresses: 199 Elm Ridge Drive, Kitchener and 86 Elgin St. S, Cambridge, for nominal consideration to The Regional Municipality of Waterloo; Direct the Chief Financial Officer to discharge the existing mortgage on title for 86 Elgin St. S, Cambridge , valued at $2,775,936 as of October 1, 2023 plus any related costs, u s ing funding from the Region’s Housing Capital Reserve; and Direct the Commissioner of Corporate Services and the Commissioner of Community Services to take all necessary actions and execute all necessary documents to complete the transfer of ownership to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor.
motions.text_html:
That the Regional Municipality of Waterloo take the following action with respect to the proposed property ownership transfer from the Region of Waterloo Community Housing Inc. to the Regional Municipality of Waterloo as set out in report CSD-HOU-23-022 dated August 15, 2023:

  1. Accept the transfer of ownership effective December 31, 2023 or sooner if practicably possible, of two (2) community housing properties comprising 92 units in total at the following addresses: 199 Elm Ridge Drive, Kitchener and 86 Elgin St. S, Cambridge, for nominal consideration to The Regional Municipality of Waterloo;

  2. Direct the Chief Financial Officer to discharge the existing mortgage on title for 86 Elgin St. S, Cambridge, valued at $2,775,936 as of October 1, 2023 plus any related costs, using funding from the Region’s Housing Capital Reserve; and

  3. Direct the Commissioner of Corporate Services and the Commissioner of Community Services to take all necessary actions and execute all necessary documents to complete the transfer of ownership to the satisfaction of the Regional Solicitor.
